explanation.why: Amazon Textract is purpose-built for extracting printed text, forms, key-value pairs, tables, invoices, and receipts from PDFs and images while preserving document structure.
keyPoints: Works with PDFs and scanned images
explanation.comparison: Textract specializes in OCR plus structure extraction, unlike generic image analysis services.

options.text: Amazon Rekognition for visual content

explanation.summary: Image analysis services do not specialize in structured document extraction.
explanation.why: Amazon Rekognition focuses on labels, faces, objects, moderation, and video/image analysis rather than extracting tables, forms, and invoice fields from documents.

options.text: Amazon Comprehend for natural language processing

explanation.summary: Natural language processing analyzes text after extraction rather than performing OCR and form extraction.
explanation.why: Amazon Comprehend processes existing text for sentiment, entities, and topics but does not extract structured content directly from PDFs or scanned images.
explanation.comparison: Textract extracts text from documents; Comprehend analyzes the extracted text.

options.text: Amazon Translate for language conversion

explanation.summary: Translation services convert text between languages rather than extracting structured documents.
explanation.why: Amazon Translate provides neural machine translation but does not detect forms, tables, invoices, or OCR document structures.

questions.question: A development team wants to know when to use Amazon Bedrock vs Amazon SageMaker for an AI workload. The team is building a customer-facing chatbot that uses an off-the-shelf foundation model with no custom training. Which service is more appropriate, and why?

options.text: SageMaker, because all production AI must use SageMaker

explanation.summary: Production AI workloads do not universally require SageMaker.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker is a comprehensive machine learning platform for building, training, tuning, and deploying custom ML models. However, simple consumption of managed foundation models without custom training is often better suited for Amazon Bedrock.
explanation.comparison: SageMaker emphasizes custom ML workflows, while Bedrock emphasizes managed foundation model access.

options.text: Bedrock, because it provides managed API access to foundation models without requiring infrastructure management or training

explanation.summary: Managed foundation model APIs simplify generative AI application development without custom training infrastructure.
explanation.why: Amazon Bedrock provides serverless access to foundation models through managed APIs. It is ideal for chatbot and generative AI applications that use pretrained models without requiring GPU management, model hosting, or custom training workflows.
keyPoints: Designed for generative AI application development
explanation.comparison: Bedrock offers direct managed FM access, while SageMaker provides full ML lifecycle tooling.

options.text: Bedrock and SageMaker are identical; use either

explanation.summary: Bedrock and SageMaker serve different AI and ML workflow purposes.
explanation.why: Amazon Bedrock focuses on managed foundation model access and generative AI APIs, while SageMaker supports end-to-end machine learning workflows including training, tuning, deployment, and MLOps.

options.text: Neither service supports this use case

explanation.summary: AWS fully supports generative AI chatbot workloads through managed AI services.
explanation.why: Amazon Bedrock is specifically designed to support chatbot and generative AI applications using managed foundation models.

questions.question: A financial services company is deploying an AI system for loan approval decisions. Compliance needs to identify the core dimensions of responsible AI the system must address. Which three dimensions are central to responsible AI per AWS guidance and broader industry frameworks? (Select three)

options.text: Fairness and bias mitigation across demographic groups

explanation.summary: Responsible AI frameworks emphasize fairness and mitigation of discriminatory outcomes.
explanation.why: AI systems used for high-impact decisions such as loan approvals must minimize unfair bias across protected demographic groups and ensure equitable treatment.
keyPoints: Bias mitigation is a core responsible AI principle

options.text: Transparency and explainability of model decisions

explanation.summary: Transparency and explainability support accountability and regulatory compliance.
explanation.why: Organizations must often explain how AI systems make decisions, especially in regulated domains like finance, healthcare, and insurance.

options.text: Maximum profit optimization at all costs

explanation.summary: Responsible AI balances business goals with ethical and regulatory considerations.
explanation.why: Responsible AI frameworks prioritize fairness, safety, transparency, accountability, and privacy rather than unrestricted profit maximization.
explanation.comparison: Business optimization must coexist with governance and ethical constraints.

options.text: Privacy and security of training and inference data

explanation.summary: Responsible AI requires protection of sensitive data throughout the AI lifecycle.
explanation.why: Financial systems process highly sensitive personal and financial information that must be protected during data collection, training, storage, inference, and monitoring.

questions.question: A team is implementing AI governance and wants to formally document each model with intended use, training data, performance, ethical considerations, and known limitations. They want an AWS service providing a centralized standardized template for this model documentation. Which service fits?

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch Logs for performance logging

explanation.summary: Operational logging services do not provide structured AI governance documentation templates.
explanation.why: Amazon CloudWatch Logs captures monitoring and operational logs rather than formal model governance documentation.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Model Registry for version tracking only

explanation.summary: Model Registry tracks model lifecycle metadata rather than comprehensive governance documentation.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker Model Registry manages model versions, approvals, and deployment stages, but it does not provide the detailed governance-focused documentation structure of Model Cards.
explanation.comparison: Model Registry manages lifecycle state; Model Cards manage governance documentation.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards for centralized model documentation

explanation.summary: Model Cards provide standardized governance documentation for machine learning models.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards help teams document intended use, training datasets, evaluation metrics, ethical considerations, limitations, and governance details in a centralized standardized format.

options.text: AWS Trusted Advisor for general recommendations

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor provides operational AWS recommendations rather than AI governance documentation.
explanation.why: AWS Trusted Advisor focuses on cost optimization, security, performance, and reliability recommendations for AWS resources.

questions.question: A team needs to detect potential bias in BOTH the training data BEFORE training and the deployed model AFTER training. They want one managed AWS service providing bias metrics across protected attributes like age, gender, and ethnicity, plus explainability of model predictions. Which service fits?

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Clarify for bias detection and explainability

explanation.summary: Bias detection and explainability tools support responsible AI governance across the ML lifecycle.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker Clarify detects bias in datasets before training, evaluates bias in model predictions after deployment, and provides explainability techniques such as SHAP-based feature attribution.
keyPoints: Bias detection before and after training

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor for production drift only

explanation.summary: Model Monitor primarily focuses on production monitoring and drift detection.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor detects data drift, model quality degradation, and feature distribution changes but does not provide the comprehensive fairness and explainability capabilities of Clarify.

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch for operational metrics

explanation.summary: Operational observability tools do not provide ML fairness analysis or explainability.
explanation.why: CloudWatch monitors infrastructure and application metrics rather than responsible AI characteristics.

options.text: AWS Config for resource configuration compliance

explanation.summary: AWS Config evaluates infrastructure compliance rather than machine learning fairness.
explanation.why: AWS Config tracks AWS resource configurations and compliance rules but does not analyze datasets, predictions, or ML bias.

questions.question: A team is debating the distinction between MODEL INTERPRETABILITY and MODEL EXPLAINABILITY. The team needs to understand the conceptual difference between these two terms in responsible AI.

options.text: The two terms mean the same thing and can be used interchangeably

explanation.summary: Interpretability and explainability are related but distinct responsible AI concepts.
explanation.why: Interpretability focuses on understanding model internals directly, while explainability often focuses on communicating understandable reasons for outputs to stakeholders.

options.text: Interpretability refers to the model's source code; explainability refers to reproducing the model's results

explanation.summary: Responsible AI definitions are not based on source code visibility or reproducibility alone.
explanation.why: Interpretability concerns understanding internal decision mechanisms, while explainability concerns communicating understandable reasoning behind outputs.

options.text: Interpretability is about understanding the INTERNAL MECHANISMS of the model itself; explainability is about providing UNDERSTANDABLE REASONS for predictions and behaviors to stakeholders, often using post-hoc techniques for complex models

explanation.summary: Interpretability focuses on model internals, while explainability focuses on understandable reasoning for outputs.
explanation.why: Interpretability refers to how directly humans can understand a model’s internal mechanisms and structure. Explainability refers to methods that communicate why predictions were made, especially for complex black-box models using techniques like SHAP or feature attribution.
keyPoints: Post-hoc explanations are common for deep learning models
examples: SHAP values improve explainability for neural networks

options.text: Interpretability is for performance; explainability is for security

explanation.summary: Interpretability and explainability relate to understanding model behavior rather than performance versus security.
explanation.why: These concepts are part of responsible AI governance and human understanding of model behavior, not separate operational domains.

questions.question: A development team is building an AI image generation feature. The team wants to ensure that generated images include a tamper-evident indicator that the image was AI-generated. Which AWS capability addresses this need?

options.text: Customer feedback forms after image use

explanation.summary: Feedback collection does not provide technical provenance or tamper evidence for generated images.
explanation.why: Customer feedback processes may help improve systems but do not embed detectable provenance indicators into generated media.

options.text: Manual photo cropping by a human reviewer

explanation.summary: Manual image editing does not provide AI provenance verification.
explanation.why: Cropping or manual review does not embed tamper-evident metadata or invisible watermarking into generated images.

options.text: Disabling all image generation

explanation.summary: Disabling functionality avoids the use case rather than implementing responsible AI safeguards.
explanation.why: The requirement is to support AI image generation with provenance and transparency controls, not eliminate the capability entirely.

options.text: Invisible watermarking on Amazon Titan Image Generator outputs

explanation.summary: Invisible watermarking supports provenance tracking and identification of AI-generated images.
explanation.why: Amazon Titan Image Generator includes invisible watermarking capabilities that embed tamper-evident indicators into generated images to support responsible AI, provenance detection, and synthetic media identification.

questions.question: A team is reviewing the AWS Shared Responsibility Model as it applies to AI on AWS. The team needs to understand which security and responsible AI tasks are typically the CUSTOMER's responsibility when using Amazon Bedrock.

options.text: Configuring IAM policies, encryption keys, VPC settings, application-level guardrails, prompt and output handling, and acceptable use policies

explanation.summary: Customers are responsible for securing their applications, identities, configurations, and responsible AI controls when using managed AI services.
explanation.why: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, AWS secures the underlying cloud infrastructure, while customers are responsible for configuring identity and access management, encryption, networking, application behavior, prompt handling, guardrails, and governance controls for their Bedrock applications.
keyPoints: Customers manage IAM and encryption settings
Application-level AI safety remains customer responsibility
explanation.comparison: AWS secures the infrastructure; customers secure their workloads and AI application behavior.

options.text: Patching the underlying operating systems of Bedrock servers

explanation.summary: Managed service infrastructure maintenance is handled by AWS.
explanation.why: Amazon Bedrock is a managed AWS service, so AWS is responsible for maintaining and patching the underlying infrastructure and operating systems.

options.text: Physical security of AWS data centers

explanation.summary: Physical infrastructure security is an AWS responsibility.
explanation.why: AWS manages the security of its facilities, hardware, and environmental protections within AWS regions and data centers.

options.text: Maintaining the global AWS network infrastructure

explanation.summary: AWS manages and secures the global cloud network infrastructure.
explanation.why: The global AWS backbone network, connectivity infrastructure, and regional networking components are maintained by AWS as part of the managed cloud platform.

questions.question: Rank these generative AI scenarios from LEAST to MOST customer security responsibility: (1) pretraining a foundation model from scratch, (2) fine-tuning an existing FM with custom data, (3) consuming a fully managed third-party generative AI service, (4) building an app calling a third-party FM.

options.text: All four scenarios involve identical customer security responsibility

explanation.summary: Customer responsibility varies significantly depending on control over the AI stack.
explanation.why: As organizations gain more control over training, customization, infrastructure, and data pipelines, their operational and security responsibilities increase.

options.text: (1) pretraining, (2) fine-tuning, (3) consuming public service, (4) building app

explanation.summary: Pretraining from scratch represents the highest customer responsibility, not the lowest.
explanation.why: Building and training foundation models from scratch requires customers to manage datasets, infrastructure, governance, security, and compliance at every layer.
explanation.comparison: Managed AI services significantly reduce operational responsibility compared to self-managed training.

options.text: (4) building app, (1) pretraining, (3) consuming service, (2) fine-tuning

explanation.summary: This ordering incorrectly places pretraining near the middle rather than the highest-responsibility position.
explanation.why: Pretraining foundation models from scratch requires the broadest operational, security, governance, and compliance ownership.

options.text: (3) consuming public service, (4) building app, (2) fine-tuning, (1) pretraining from scratch

explanation.summary: Customer security responsibility increases as control and customization of AI systems increase.
explanation.why: Using a fully managed public AI service requires the least responsibility because the provider handles most infrastructure and model management. Building applications introduces application-level security responsibility. Fine-tuning adds responsibility for custom training data and model adaptation. Pretraining foundation models from scratch requires full ownership of datasets, infrastructure, governance, training security, and compliance.
keyPoints: Managed services minimize customer operational burden

questions.question: A team is implementing a defense-in-depth approach for a generative AI application on AWS. The team needs to combine multiple layers of protection rather than relying on a single control. Which strategy aligns with the defense-in-depth principle?

options.text: Applying multiple layers of security measures including input validation, access controls, encryption, monitoring, and AI-specific guardrails

explanation.summary: Defense-in-depth uses multiple overlapping protections to reduce the impact of individual control failures.
explanation.why: A layered security strategy combines identity controls, encryption, monitoring, validation, network protections, and AI-specific safeguards such as guardrails and moderation filters. This reduces the likelihood that a single weakness compromises the system.
explanation.comparison: Defense-in-depth uses overlapping controls instead of relying on one security mechanism.

options.text: Implementing a single perimeter firewall to block all attacks

explanation.summary: Defense-in-depth requires multiple layers rather than a single security boundary.
explanation.why: Modern threats can bypass individual controls, so relying solely on a perimeter firewall creates a single point of failure.

options.text: Relying solely on data encryption to address all risks

explanation.summary: Encryption is important but cannot mitigate all security and AI risks alone.
explanation.why: Encryption protects confidentiality but does not address prompt injection, identity compromise, harmful outputs, or application vulnerabilities.
explanation.comparison: Defense-in-depth combines encryption with many additional security layers.

options.text: Using one authentication mechanism for all users and services

explanation.summary: Authentication is only one component of a broader layered security strategy.
explanation.why: Defense-in-depth requires multiple complementary controls beyond authentication alone, including authorization, monitoring, segmentation, and AI-specific protections.

questions.question: A team is using a foundation model on Amazon Bedrock to generate marketing content. The team needs to address copyright and intellectual property concerns about AI-generated outputs. Which approach aligns with responsible AI practices for IP and copyright?

options.text: Publish all AI outputs without review, assuming no IP risk exists

explanation.summary: AI-generated outputs can still create legal, compliance, and reputational risks requiring oversight.
explanation.why: Organizations should review generated outputs for copyright, trademark, brand, and regulatory risks rather than assuming all generated content is automatically safe.

options.text: Review AWS Service Terms and Amazon Bedrock model-provider terms for applicable IP indemnification and copyright-risk coverage, establish internal review processes for AI-generated content, retain human oversight for IP-sensitive material, and document the model and version used

explanation.summary: Responsible AI governance for IP risk combines contractual review, human oversight, and documented controls.
explanation.why: Organizations should understand AWS and provider-specific terms, establish review and approval processes, retain human oversight for sensitive content, document model provenance, and implement governance controls to manage copyright and intellectual property risks.
examples: Tracking model versions for generated assets
explanation.comparison: Responsible AI governance manages risk rather than assuming risk-free generation.

options.text: Train the model on copyrighted material without any review or controls

explanation.summary: Uncontrolled use of copyrighted material violates responsible AI governance principles.
explanation.why: Organizations should apply governance, licensing review, and legal controls when handling copyrighted training data and generated outputs.

options.text: Avoid using foundation models entirely to eliminate all risk

explanation.summary: Responsible AI focuses on risk management and governance rather than avoiding AI adoption entirely.
explanation.why: Organizations can responsibly deploy generative AI by implementing oversight, governance, documentation, and review controls instead of eliminating useful technologies altogether.
